# As Promised: My Top 5 Kids and Money Apps (and they’re all FREE!)

![Father and child looking at phone and laughing](https://cdn-ilebcba.nitrocdn.com/AdIJHkVeVzXGtXNOqSTngKRIHCyosZAe/assets/images/optimized/rev-2075a11/fearlessfinance.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/as-promised-scaled.jpg)

As always, I have strong reservations about money and apps because people tend to abandon them after the first try or two. However, if you want an app to track your child’s chores to earn extra money then these can be very useful.  I like that you can **designate savings, charity and spending** on many of them to **get your child thinking about the many “pots”** we put our money in, but the rub is that the actual green money will reside in a piggy bank or drawer or wherever it is.

If your child is not **diligent in getting you to fill in the app or filling in the app herself**, she might not be able to hold herself back from spending all the green money in her real piggy bank. **I suggest having 3 actual piggy banks to correlate with the saving, spending and charity virtual ones.**

I believe the great thing apps can teach is **how to handle money**(K12 Money!), how to **understand the relationship between work and pay**(Chorepay) and how to **see your progress saving** for something you want (P2K, IAllowance). Another critical lesson is learning what **keeping track of a virtual checkbook** is like by having to input deposits or withdrawals (bankaroo). **Experiencing how you can be left with zero** (or negative) in your account is also good life lesson.

- [P2K](https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/p2k-money/id405631656?mt=8) – FREE– Best for a kid who is 7 or 8 yrs old and kids manage the app. **P2K is a kids’ budgeting tool**. It creates a very simple **introduction to “income” and “expense”** by asking your child to input allowance as “income” and buying a toy as an “expense.” Kids can save for things on their wishlist, and see their progress toward having enough to buy the toy.
- [K12 Money](https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/k12-money/id425743471?mt=8) – FREE – Start your kids in Kindergarten or first grade.  This app will help your kids with **math, money and analytical skills**. It’s a winner! Bills and coins, **make change, matching, counting**. Everything you need to teach your child the math of money. K12 coins is just coins, but get the K12 Money app because you can set it to just coins if you want.
- [Iallowance](https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/iallowance-lt-allowances-chores/id465959056?mt=8) – FREE – Start 5 or 6 year olds depending on their comfort with numbers and use it with your child. **Track allowance, gifts, and chores**.  Use time, money, and stars as “payment.”  You need an upgrade for more than 2 chores and few other goodies.  Your child can have **piggy banks for saving, giving or spending**. Set up  other “banks” for special items like a specific toy.
- [Bankaroo](https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/bankaroo-mobile/id504924470?mt=8) – FREE – has a website and app.  Best for kids 7 & up and kids manage the app. **Wishlist allows a kid to see what saving towards one item** looks like.  She can put part of her allowance toward it each week or a one-off payment.  She subtracts the funds when she buys it, like a checkbook.
- [Chorepay](https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/chorepay/id503507607?mt=8) – FREE – Use with your child starting at 5 or 6 yrs old. An **allowance-for-chores tracker** for you and your child.  Good user interface and you can designate donate, save, spend and credit.  Good visual interface for younger kids.

# The   easiest   way to keep track of money for kids

You pay for items kids buy, then deduct in the app. Add birthday money and allowances. More convenient than cash, less hassle than bank accounts.


[![Download on the App Store](https://toolbox.marketingtools.apple.com/api/v2/badges/download-on-the-app-store/black/en-us?releaseDate=1679788800)](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/piggy-bank-kids-bomad/id6446114229?itscg=30200&itsct=apps_box_badge&mttnsubad=6446114229)

[![Get it on Google Play](https://play.google.com/intl/en_us/badges/static/images/badges/en_badge_web_generic.png)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=app.bomad&utm_source=website&pcampaignid=pcampaignidMKT-Other-global-all-co-prtnr-py-PartBadge-Mar2515-1)

![](https://bomad.app/images/home/girl-and-phone.webp)

Bomad, short for Bank of Mom and Dad, lets parents run **virtual bank accounts** for their kids, avoiding the hassle of cash and real bank accounts.

Kids can see their **balances** and **transactions** in the kids app on their own devices, and they receive
**notifications** too.

Bomad can be used as an [allowance tracker](https://bomad.app/allowance-tracker), [piggy bank](https://bomad.app/piggy-bank-app) or [pocket money app](https://bomad.app/pocket-money-app). It's the best alternative to [Bankaroo](https://bomad.app/bankaroo).

# The Best Budgeting Apps for New Parents

## Having a budget—like having a baby—is the ultimate in adulting. These apps make it easy.

![author-Katrina Nattress](https://images.ctfassets.net/50gzycvace50/6F0Jvt38m0W9jbN0mroaYO/ca8b562acc34dbf38d5e7a31327be4da/KatrinaNattress_July2019_IMG_9969_JasonQuigley.jpg?w=48)

###### By [Katrina Nattress](https://www.babylist.com/hello-baby/authors/katrina-nattress)

###### Fact Checked by [Shannon Vestal Robson](https://www.babylist.com/hello-baby/authors/shannon-robson)

Updated On Mar 25, 2026

Updated On Mar 25, 2026

Our editors independently test and curate products. If you make a purchase via our links we may earn a commission.

Having a baby comes with a whole lot of “firsts,” and for many soon-to-be parents, one of those is [creating a budget for the first time](https://www.babylist.com/hello-baby/how-to-make-a-family-budget). If the thought of creating a budget makes you feel a little uneasy, you’re not alone. The [cost of having a baby](https://www.babylist.com/hello-baby/cost-of-raising-a-baby) may be overwhelming on its own, and throwing all your other finances into the mix takes it to a whole other level. This might be the first time you’ve really had to sit down and make a budget, and if you’re unsure where to start, we’re here to help.

R.J. Weiss, a Certified Financial Planner and [founder of The Ways to Wealth](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thewaystowealth.com%2F&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown), recommends preparing your finances before the baby comes. “Prioritize saving for peace of mind and create a solid financial plan,” the father of three advises. “Major changes will be hard to implement once the baby is here, so having a plan will help you manage unexpected expenses and reduce financial stress during this new phase of life.”

Budgeting apps are an easy way to start creating your budget and monitoring expenses (even those [future ones like childcare](https://www.babylist.com/hello-baby/low-cost-child-care)). They can also be an excellent companion to larger financial planning goals if you’ve already begun budgeting efforts. There are _so many_ apps on the market, and many specialize in specific budgeting methods or cater to particular aspects of finances, from savings goals to investments. We spoke to several financial experts about what apps they personally use and selected the cream of the crop for new parents. We even broke down and categorized each app to help you find the perfect one for your growing family.

## Babylist’s Picks for the Best Budgeting Apps

## Best All-In-One Budgeting App

![Monarch](https://images.ctfassets.net/50gzycvace50/mbtL33ToMuUbFdqu6RS1w/7b3924705c5c809f820d1971e774fbc0/Screenshot_2025-08-07_at_1.58.32_PM.png)

### Monarch

[iOS](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fapps.apple.com%252Fus%252Fapp%252Fmonarch-money%252Fid1459319842%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "Monarch") \| [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.monarchmoney.mobile "Monarch")

If you’re looking to go all in with your financial planning, [Monarch](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fmonarchmoney.sjv.io%2F3JRRQr%3FsubId1%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown%26u%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.monarchmoney.com%252Flanding%252Fbabylist&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "Monarch") is a comprehensive and customizable app that does it all for you. It syncs with your bank accounts, credit cards, loans and investments, and automatically categorizes transactions in your budget. The app also boasts a number of other features, reports and tools, including the ability to add family members to your account at no additional cost.

Weiss personally uses Monarch to keep his household finances in order. “It’s simple to use and does a great job of helping me keep track of the family budget,” he says.

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| **Cost** | $14.99/month; $99/year |

## Best Zero-Based Budgeting App

![YNAB](https://images.ctfassets.net/50gzycvace50/iCFDhT1qFFo7UyOjZr6So/dc50893ae9523328415f645f3f6f4c1e/YNAB.webp)

### YNAB (You Need A Budget)

[iOS](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fapps.apple.com%252Fus%252Fapp%252Fynab%252Fid1010865877%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown) \| [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.youneedabudget.evergreen.app)

[YNAB](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.ynab.com%252F%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "YNAB (You Need A Budget)") uses the [zero-based budgeting strategy](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.fidelity.com%252Flearning-center%252Fsmart-money%252Fzero-based-budgeting%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "Zero-based budgeting strategy"), which means every dollar earned is assigned to a specific part of your budget, including saving and investing. The app allows you to share your plan with family members and not only syncs transactions but also features smart categorization that learns your spending habits over time.

YNAB’s interface can be a little more challenging to navigate, but the reward is worth it for serious users. “It takes a time commitment to set up and utilize properly, but if you are committed, it can turn your financial life around,” says [FutureMoney](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.futuremoney.co%252F%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "FutureMoney") co-founder Dave Fortin.

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| **Cost** | $14.99/month; $99/year |

## Best Budgeting App If You’re a Financial Novice

![EveryDollar](https://images.ctfassets.net/50gzycvace50/7Gewpao2KCwvSTWe5eoL8r/98ea85d4c6c1bfe68591b6d6322f43ed/EveryDollar.webp)

### EveryDollar

[iOS](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fapps.apple.com%252Fus%252Fapp%252Feverydollar-personal-budget%252Fid942571931%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown) \| [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.everydollar.android)

If you’re interested in the zero-based budgeting strategy but don’t want to pay the fee for an app like YNAB, [EveryDollar](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.ramseysolutions.com%252Framseyplus%252Feverydollar%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "EveryDollar") implements the same method of assigning every penny a job in your budget, but offers a free version. In the free app, users manually input income and expenses, but if manual input becomes too tedious, the premium version allows you to link to your bank accounts for automatic synching, among other tools.

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| **Cost** | Free (Premium version: $17.99/month; $79.99/year) |

## Best Budgeting App That’s Also a Joint Bank Account

![Zeta](https://images.ctfassets.net/50gzycvace50/5ubnTo8IExEe0jiWDxoxug/c9a56ac5e6b826f589cf48b221af4934/Zeta.webp)

### Zeta

[iOS](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fapps.apple.com%252Fus%252Fapp%252Fzeta-joint-card%252Fid1493011848%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown) \| [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.askzeta.aZetaFi)

[Zeta](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.askzeta.com%252F%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown) is a double whammy for parents who want to share a bank account in addition to sharing a budget. The app champions itself as being designed for families and allows you to pay bills (there’s even a bill calendar), track shared spending and make savings goals all in one place. Another perk? Zeta’s totally free to use. That being said, the app does offer a premium version that allows additional users (four instead of three) and custom automations for bills and savings goals.

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| **Cost** | Free (Premium version: $6.99/month) |

## Best Budgeting App If You’re Saving For a Goal

![Quapital](https://images.ctfassets.net/50gzycvace50/76c4zq2PT55xdgsZDKkVtY/e3a3e21eff7f396131fe3aa6dee9592e/Quapital.webp)

### Qapital

[iOS](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fapps.apple.com%252Fus%252Fapp%252Fqapital-set-forget-finances%252Fid969977669%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown) \| [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.qapital)

[Qapital](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.qapital.com%252F%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "Qapital") is the perfect app for anyone who likes to save for a specific goal. “As a new parent, you have a lot of needs, and this app helps you prioritize those financial objectives,” says money expert and [journalist Andrea Woroch](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fandreaworoch.com%252F%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "Andrea Woroch"). “This could include saving for college, family vacays and upgrading your car or buying a bigger home.”

Qapital calls its primary tool “set-and-forget saving” because users are able to link their bank account, set goals, create rules (i.e., $50 a month goes into a new house fund) and let the app do the rest. Qapital offers a tiered membership plan that includes features like a Qapital debit card, a cash tracking tool and investment options; however, even Basic members are able to add a partner to their plan for shared savings goals.

## Best Digital Envelope Budgeting App

![GoodBudget](https://images.ctfassets.net/50gzycvace50/6CEnJezbUAcOK52owRIPga/6fe2d67bdc9caa5cf04d0d1cfe69e10f/GoodBudget.webp)

### GoodBudget

[iOS](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fapps.apple.com%252Fus%252Fapp%252Fgoodbudget-budget-planner%252Fid471112395%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown) \| [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.dayspringtech.envelopes)

[GoodBudget](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fgoodbudget.com%252F%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "GoodBudget") implements a digital version of the [cash envelope system](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fgoodbudget.com%252Fenvelope-budgeting%252F%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "Envelope Budgeting"), which is when you allocate a specific amount to different expense categories to ensure you don’t overspend, and then gives you a clear picture of how much you saved when you underspend.

“New parents have many new expenses to prepare for, and this can make budgeting more difficult. \[The\] envelope method keeps everything organized and helps you \[better\] prepare your finances each month,” explains Woroch. “You then use that money to pay bills or \[make\] purchases that fit within the category, which can help keep you to your spending plan without much thought.”

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| **Cost** | $10/month; $80/year |

## Best Customizable Budgeting App

![PocketGuard](https://images.ctfassets.net/50gzycvace50/5mgPfg8GKxUXz00xSYe9qU/4c681e9ce49815bf6b887bd5266a3bb5/PocketGuard.webp)

### PocketGuard

[iOS](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fapps.apple.com%252Fus%252Fapp%252Fpocketguard-money-bill-tracker%252Fid949414211%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown) \| [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pocketguard.android.app)

There are a number of different budgeting methods that certain apps specialize in, but [PocketGuard](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fpocketguard.com%252F%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "PocketGuard") allows you to choose any rule you want, including zero-based budgeting, the digital envelope system and the [50/30/20 method](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.nerdwallet.com%252Farticle%252Ffinance%252Fnerdwallet-budget-calculator%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown), where 50% of your budget goes to needs, 30% goes to wants and 20% goes to savings. Users are able to link bank accounts, and PocketGuard will notify you if you’re close to going over your budgeting goal. It also offers insights on ways to change spending habits, as well as debt payoff plans and savings goals, but perhaps its most popular feature is [“In My Pocket”](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fhelp.pocketguard.com%252Fhc%252Fen-us%252Farticles%252F360002167320-IN-MY-POCKET%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "“In My Pocket”"): a digital snapshot of how much money you’ll have leftover after paying your bills, budgets, goals and debts.

| **Cost** | Free (Premium version: $12.99/month; $74.99/year) |

## Best Budgeting App For DIY Investors

![Empower](https://images.ctfassets.net/50gzycvace50/6AnxulqG9gC4q40r9PWnxM/3b03d518073840df7d388d25b0d80fd4/Empower.webp)

### Empower

[iOS](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fapps.apple.com%252Fus%252Fapp%252Fempower%252Fid1001257338%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown) \| [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.participantmobileapp)

For some parents, investing is an important piece to the budgeting puzzle, and [Empower](https://redirect.viglink.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredirect.viglink.com%3Fu%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.empower.com%252F%26key%3Db1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92%26cuid%3Dbl-anon-guides-markdown&key=b1ea3950e6f8c7c04e5ec6ec113c4f92&cuid=bl-anon-guides-markdown "Empower") boasts tools to manage both. The app allows you to view your spending, bank accounts, mortgage, investments and retirement accounts all in one place. It also includes budgeting features that allow you to set savings goals and gives insight on where you can cut costs in order to maximize your savings. It’s worth noting that the investment function is the emphasis of Empower, so this app is best for DIY investors who’d like a big picture view of their finances.

We look at the best money & budgeting apps, how they work, and specific features to look out for when deciding what's suitable for your child.

Related: [Teaching kids about money](https://www.gohenry.com/uk/blog/financial-education/ways-to-teach-kids-about-money), [Budgeting for kids](https://www.gohenry.com/uk/blog/financial-education/what-is-a-fun-way-to-teach-budgeting-to-your-child-money-missions), [Budgeting for teens](https://www.gohenry.com/uk/blog/financial-education/how-to-teach-your-teenager-about-budgeting)

[Start your kids’ money journey today!](https://www.gohenry.com/uk/kids-debit-card/)

## What are the benefits of budgeting & money apps for kids & teens?

Money and budgeting apps are fantastic tools to help your child keep track of their finances and understand how much they spend. Not only will the right app help your child to stick to a budget, but it will also help them to learn to manage their money.

Beth Zemble, VP for Education at GoHenry, agrees, "There are many activities that can help kids understand the tenets of financial education, but the most important things to teach kids about from a young age are the value of money and how to make good spending decisions."

Using a money app will also [help you talk to kids about money](https://www.gohenry.com/uk/blog/financial-education/how-to-talk-to-your-kids-about-money) with real-world examples. Not only can you show them the importance of budgeting, but talking about money is a great way to see if your child is ready for a prepaid debit card.

Related: [Financial literacy for kids](https://www.gohenry.com/uk/blog/financial-education/financial-literacy-for-kids-why-is-it-important), [Money management for teens](https://www.gohenry.com/uk/blog/financial-education/teaching-teens-about-money-management)

## How do budgeting & money apps work?

A budgeting & money app is a mobile app that helps kids learn to manage their finances. These apps can be used for a variety of purposes, including pocket money, tracking spending, budgeting, saving, and organising your money. Money apps can be a great way to engage kids in learning more about money and money management. They can do this in a variety of ways, but most commonly, they will:

- Connect to all accounts automatically and import transactions.

- Allow the user to enter transactions manually.

- Categorise spending so your child can see where money is going.

- Set budgets and track your child's progress towards their budgeting goals.


The best thing about these apps is they can help kids and teens track their spending more accurately than if they were to do it manually. The apps also provide insights into spending habits that your kids may have yet to be aware of and help identify areas where your kids can cut back and save more money.

Money apps for kids have strong security features, such as PINs, passwords, and two-factor authentication. This helps to protect your child's account from unauthorised access. They also offer parental controls that allow you to set spending limits, block certain websites and apps, and view your child's spending history. Using one also gives you a great opportunity to talk to your kids about [safety tips and keeping their money safe online](https://www.gohenry.com/uk/blog/online-safety/money-safety-tips-teaching-kids-to-keep-their-money-safe).

Our research shows that kids who learn about money at a young age are more likely to make better financial decisions than adults. Our research in partnership with [Censuswide and Development Economics](https://www.gohenry.com/uk/blog/financial-education/financial-education-could-double-your-childs-earning-power) shows that 77% of adults earning between £55,001 and £65,000 per year received financial education as a child.

[Financial literacy is also important for kids](https://www.gohenry.com/uk/blog/financial-education/financial-literacy-for-kids-why-is-it-important), as children who learn to manage their money are more likely to avoid debt, save for retirement, and build wealth. That’s why money apps are an excellent way for kids to learn about money management, earn money, track spending, and stay safe. They are also a great way to start conversations with your child about the value of money, spending and saving. Whichever app you decide to use, be sure to talk to them about how to use it responsibly and make wise spending decisions.

Teaching kids about money has taken on new complexity in our digital age. While previous generations learned financial basics through piggy banks and cash allowances, today’s parents are turning to technology to help children understand modern money management and develop a better relationship with the screens they are so often glued to.

Digital budgeting tools now enable kids to experience real-world financial decisions — from setting savings goals to tracking spending — all under parental supervision. These digital tools do more than just track dollars. They create natural and often fun opportunities for families to discuss spending habits, savings goals and smart financial choices.

## What to know about family money apps

As digital payments and online banking become the norm, traditional methods of teaching financial literacy need a refresh. Family money apps help bridge this gap, offering several advantages:

- **Encourage financial independence:** These apps create a safe space for children to practice money management skills while parents maintain oversight. Kids can make real financial decisions — like choosing to save or spend their allowance — building practical knowledge through hands-on experience.
- **Build financial literacy:** Many apps incorporate learning through interactive features, games and age-appropriate lessons that help children grasp key money concepts naturally.
- **Simplify allowance systems:** Parents can easily manage allowances, set up chore rewards or help children budget their funds digitally, making the process simpler for both parents and kids.
- **Offer learning opportunities:** When parents can see their children’s spending patterns in real-time, it creates natural moments to discuss financial choices and guide better decisions.
- **Improve relationship with technology:** Modern parents are constantly trying to peel their kids away from screens. However, money apps can create an engaging yet educational experience that begins to introduce your child to the idea that screens can be used for more than just video games and movies.

One of the most valuable aspects of these apps is how they turn abstract money concepts into tangible experiences. When children actively participate in decisions about saving, spending or donating their own money, they develop a deeper understanding of financial responsibility. This hands-on approach helps them grasp the real value of money and learn to set meaningful financial goals.

## The best money apps for families

With numerous [family budgeting apps](https://www.bankrate.com/personal-finance/money-management-apps-for-families/) available, finding the right fit depends on your family’s needs and children’s ages. Here’s a breakdown for parents to help narrow down the decision:

### 1\. BusyKid — Best for allowance management

BusyKid takes a practical approach to teaching kids about earning money. The app connects chores with earnings, helping children understand the relationship between work and rewards. Beyond basic allowance tracking, BusyKid introduces children to real-world money management through its prepaid debit card option, which lets them use their earnings within parent-set boundaries.

**Key features:**

- Clear tracking system for chores and allowance
- Parent notifications for spending activity
- Options for saving, spending or exploring basic investing

What stands out about BusyKid is its introduction to investing — children can learn about the stock market with real (but parent-supervised) investments. This early exposure to investing concepts helps kids understand ideas like long-term growth and financial risk in a controlled environment.

### 2\. Greenlight — Best for teens

[Greenlight](https://www.bankrate.com/credit-cards/reviews/greenlight-debit-card/) strikes a balance between teenage independence and parental oversight. The app allows teens to develop financial decision-making skills while keeping parents in the loop. This approach works particularly well for families looking to give their teenagers more financial responsibility without removing safety nets entirely.

**Key features:**

- Customizable spending controls, including store-specific limits
- Instant transaction alerts and balance updates
- Educational resources focused on teen financial literacy

The app’s investment features and comprehensive educational content make it particularly valuable for teens who are ready to learn about more advanced financial concepts, such as long-term savings strategies and investment basics.

### 3\. FamZoo – Best for multiple children

Think of FamZoo as your family’s private banking system. The app excels at helping parents manage multiple children’s accounts while teaching everyone about household finances. Its straightforward approach makes it easier for families to create a unified system for allowances, savings and spending.

**Key features:**

- Separate account tracking for each child
- Flexible options for prepaid cards or digital IOU tracking
- Customizable spending categories for different age groups

FamZoo’s strength lies in its ability to adapt to different family situations while maintaining consistent financial teaching. Its family-centered approach is perfect for households with more than one child, as it creates a team environment around [budgeting and savings](https://www.bankrate.com/banking/savings/ways-to-save-money-on-a-tight-budget/).

GoHenry places learning at the forefront, making it particularly effective for younger children just starting their financial journey. The app combines practical money management tools with educational content that grows with your child.

The app’s focus on building foundational money knowledge through interactive learning makes it especially valuable for families with younger children who are just beginning to understand financial concepts.

## Key considerations for choosing the right app

Every family has unique financial teaching needs. Here’s what to consider when selecting an app that fits your household:

- **Age-appropriate design:** Match the app’s features with your child’s understanding level. Younger children benefit from simple, visual interfaces focused on basic concepts, while teens need tools that can handle more complex financial decisions.
- **Cost and fees:** While most family finance apps charge monthly or annual fees, their costs vary significantly. Consider whether premium features — like additional educational content or specialized [debit card](https://www.bankrate.com/banking/checking/how-to-get-a-debit-card/) services — align with your family’s goals and budget.
- **Customization options:** Look for apps with adjustable settings that can evolve with your child. Features like customizable chore lists, adjustable spending limits and expanding educational content help ensure the app remains useful as your child develops financial independence.
- **Educational approach:** Consider how each app teaches financial concepts. Some focus on learning through daily transactions, while others offer structured lessons about topics ranging from basic budgeting to [understanding interest rates](https://www.bankrate.com/banking/savings/what-is-interest/).
- **Security features:** Prioritize apps with robust security measures, including parent-controlled accounts and secure transaction monitoring, to ensure safe financial learning.

## Encouraging financial conversations at home

While apps provide valuable tools, meaningful family discussions about money create lasting financial wisdom. Here are five natural ways to incorporate money talks into daily life:

### Use everyday moments as teaching tools

Turn regular activities into learning opportunities. Whether you’re comparing prices at the grocery store or deciding on a family purchase, share your thinking process. These real-world scenarios help children connect financial decisions with actual outcomes.

### Create shared financial goals

Work together on family savings projects, like planning a special trip or saving for a shared purchase. This collaborative approach shows children how individual choices contribute to larger financial goals and teaches the value of working together.

### Support individual money goals

Help your children identify and work toward personal financial targets, whether saving for a special item or setting aside money for charity. Using family finance apps to visualize progress can make abstract concepts like delayed gratification more concrete.

### Show financial responsibility in action

Children learn by example. Share appropriate financial decisions you make, explaining your thought process for saving, budgeting or planning larger purchases. When facing financial challenges, discuss them in age-appropriate ways to demonstrate realistic money management.

### Make financial check-ins a routine

Set aside time each month for casual family discussions about finances. Keep these talks positive and age-appropriate, gradually introducing more sophisticated concepts as your children grow. These conversations help normalize money discussions and keep financial education an ongoing process.

## The bottom line

Today’s digital-first world requires a fresh approach to teaching children about money. While family finance apps offer valuable tools for hands-on learning, they work best as part of a broader strategy that includes open discussions and real-world practice.

Success comes from finding the right balance — using digital tools to provide practical experience while maintaining active family conversations about money. By combining thoughtful app selection with regular financial discussions, parents can help their children develop the knowledge and confidence they need for [lifelong financial well-being](https://www.bankrate.com/personal-finance/ways-to-achieve-lifelong-financial-wellness/).

## Frequently asked questions

- ### What is the best age to teach financial literacy?

Caret Down Icon




The best age to begin teaching financial literacy can be as early as three to five years old. More generally, once your child starts to verbally express their wants and needs, they become an active participant in everyday transactions — and how you respond in those moments plays a key role in shaping their understanding of money and value.



For example, if they want a chocolate bar, it’s important to show them that crying — a method that may have worked as a baby — is no longer effective. Instead, they can learn that completing chores or meeting other expectations helps them earn what they want.



The financial literacy apps mentioned above can provide helpful structure as you guide your child through these lessons that may last a lifetime.

- ### What is the 50/30/20 budget rule for kids?

Caret Down Icon




The 50/30/20 budget rule is a popular money management strategy that can be used by kids and adults alike. It suggests dividing your income into three categories: 50 percent for needs, 30 percent for wants and 20 percent for savings.



For kids, this might look like setting aside half of their allowance for essentials like school supplies or lunch money, 30 percent for fun purchases like toys or treats, and 20 percent for future goals.

Opinions are the author's alone, and this content has not been provided by, reviewed, approved or endorsed by any advertiser. Information shared on this site is for entertainment purposes only and should not be considered as professional advice. 20shares - [Share](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fmarriagekidsandmoney.com%2Fbest-budget-apps-for-families%2F&t=10%20Best%20Budget%20Apps%20for%20Families%20and%20Couples%20%282025%20Guide%29 "Share on Facebook") - [Tweet](https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=10%20Best%20Budget%20Apps%20for%20Families%20and%20Couples%20%282025%20Guide%29&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmarriagekidsandmoney.com%2Fbest-budget-apps-for-families%2F&via=AndyHillMKM "Share on X") - Pin20 - [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmarriagekidsandmoney.com%2Fbest-budget-apps-for-families%2F&title=10%20Best%20Budget%20Apps%20for%20Families%20and%20Couples%20%282025%20Guide%29&summary=Budgeting%20is%20one%20of%20the%20best%20ways%20to%20create%20financial%20stability%20in%20your%20life%20and%20protect%20your%20family%E2%80%99s%20future.%20By%20setting%20a%20plan%20and%20sticking%20to%20it%2C%20you%20can%20pay%20bills%20on%20time%2C%20build%20an&mini=true "Share on LinkedIn") Budgeting is one of the best ways to create financial stability in your life and protect your family’s future. By setting a plan and sticking to it, you can pay bills on time, build an emergency fund, eliminate debt, and invest with confidence. And thanks to today’s tech, tracking your expenses couldn’t be simpler. Whether you’re budgeting with your spouse, your kids, or even extended family, there are tools designed to make the process easier. In this guide, we’ll walk through the best budget apps for families and couples in 2025. Each one offers shared access, helpful features, and flexible pricing so you can find the right fit for your household. ## Quick Comparison of the Best Budget Apps If you want a side-by-side look, here’s how the top budget apps for families compare. This chart highlights the features that matter most: shared access, kid-friendly tools, mobile app availability, price, and who each app is best for. | App | Shared Access | Kids Features | Mobile App | Price | Best For | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [**Monarch Money**](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/monarchmoney) | ✔ Unlimited household logins | ✘ | ✔ iOS & Android | $14.99/mo or $99/yr
**7-day free trial** | Best overall for families | | [**YNAB**](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/ynab) | ✔ YNAB Together (up to 6 users) | ✘ | ✔ iOS & Android | $14.99/mo or $109/yr
**34-day free trial** | Power users | | [**Simplifi by Quicken**](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/simplifi) | ✔ Partner sharing | ✘ | ✔ iOS & Android | $5.99/mo or $47.88/yr
**30-day free trial** | Simplicity for couples | | [**Crew**](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/crew) | ✔ Family accounts | ✔ Kids’ debit cards, pockets, allowances | ✔ iOS & Android | **Free basic plan** | Families with kids
_(Note: I am a minority shareholder in Crew)_ | | [**EveryDollar**](https://www.ramseysolutions.com/ramseyplus/everydollar) | ✔ Partner sharing | ✘ | ✔ iOS & Android | **Free basic**
**14-day free trial Premium** | Dave Ramsey followers | | [**Lunch Money**](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/lunchmoney) | ✔ Invite collaborators | ✘ | ✔ iOS & Android companion app | $10/mo or $100/yr
**Free trial available** | Modern spenders | | [**Tiller**](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/tiller) | ✔ Share Google Sheets/Excel | ✘ | Via Sheets/Excel apps | $79/yr
**30-day free trial** | Spreadsheet lovers | | [**Origin**](https://www.useorigin.com/) | ✔ Couples mode | ✘ | ✔ iOS & Android | $13/mo or $156/yr
**Free trial available** | Couples wanting guidance | | [**Rocket Money**](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/rocketmoney) | ✔ Premium partner sharing | ✘ | ✔ iOS & Android | **Free basic**
Premium $4–$12/mo | Subscription tracking | | [**Spreadsheets (Google Sheets / Excel)**](https://www.google.com/sheets/about/) | ✔ Shareable files | ✘ | Via Sheets/Excel apps | **Free** | DIY, intentional budgeting | _Disclosure: Some of the links in this table are affiliate links. This means I may earn a commission if you_ _sign up through my link, at no extra cost to you. These recommendations are based on research, testing, and_ _feedback from families in the Marriage Kids and Money community. I only highlight tools I believe could be_ _genuinely helpful for families looking to budget together._ ## 1\. Monarch Money ![Monarch Money Hero](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Monarch-Hero-2024-1-1024x576.png) Monarch Money is a powerful tool for all users! Whether you're single or a couple, you’ll find this platform equally effective. Adding other household members (partners, adult kids, even parents living with you) comes at no extra cost. You can also control what data is shared as “household” versus private, which makes it flexible for different needs. Beyond budgeting, Monarch Money tracks spending, analyzes recurring expenses, monitors goals, calculates net worth, and even offers financial advice. It’s available both as a web platform and a mobile app for iOS and Android. **Best Features** - Fully customizable dashboard - Unlimited household logins with separate credentials - Read-only access and bank-level security - Goal-focused planning and progress tracking - Ad-free with no product upselling **Things to Consider** - Could expand support for more cryptocurrency exchanges (currently supports Coinbase only) **Price** - $14.99 per month or $99 annually (after a free 7-day trial) 👉 [Start your **7-day free trial** and get 50% off your first year](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/monarchmoney) 👉 Want a deeper dive? [Read our full Monarch Money Review](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/monarch-money-review/). **Why We Use It** Nicole and I have used Monarch for over two years. What sold us was how much easier it made our budgeting conversations. I used to schedule “ [budget parties](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/podcast/how-to-throw-a-budget-party-with-your-spouse/)” (yes, I really called them that) and Nicole would roll her eyes. She didn’t care about all the spreadsheets and data — she wanted to focus on what money could _do_ for our family. Monarch bridges that gap perfectly. It keeps me happy with the data while giving her a clear, emotional connection to our goals. ## 2\. YNAB (You Need a Budget) [![YNAB](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Screen-Shot-2022-09-19-at-2.59.14-PM-1024x512.jpg)](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/ynab) YNAB is one of the most popular budgeting tools out there, known for its proactive four-rule budgeting method. It offers robust features and is beloved by power users. **Best Features** - Ad-free - Real-time syncing across devices - Smart transaction categorization - Multiple budgets at once - Goal setting with targets - Loan calculator and spending reports - YNAB Together (share with up to 6 people) **Things to Consider** - Pricier than many competitors - Steeper learning curve — some users give up before it clicks **Price** - $14.99 per month or $109 per year (after a free 34-day trial) 👉 [Try YNAB free for **34 days**](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/ynab) 👉 Want a deeper dive? [Read our full YNAB Review](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/ynab-review/). **Why I Struggled With It** I gave YNAB a try back in 2018, and even after attending their free training sessions (with a very kind coach), it just didn’t click for me. I tried again in 2023 when Mint shut down, but Monarch was simply easier. That said, many in the MKM community (including my friend [Kathryn Hanna](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/author/kathrynhanna/)) swear by YNAB and love its proactive style. ## 3\. Simplifi by Quicken ![Simplifi by Quicken](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/QuickenSimplifi2.jpg) Simplifi, created by the folks behind Quicken, is designed to keep budgeting simple. It gives couples and families a clear overview of spending, goals, and cash flow without overwhelming them. **Best Features** - Automated account tracking - Real-time alerts - Built-in goal tracking - Shared partner access - Projected cash flow tools **Things to Consider** - No free trial (though discounts are common) - Lacks credit score monitoring **Price** - $5.99 per month (with discounts available) 👉 [Try Simplifi with a **30-day free trial**](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/simplifi) 👉 Want a deeper dive? [Read our full Simplifi Review](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/simplifi-review/). **Why We Like It** My friend Justine Nelson from _[Debt Free Millennials](https://www.youtube.com/c/DebtFreeMillennials)_ is a huge Simplifi fan, and I trust her expertise. I tried it myself and was impressed by how clean and simple it felt. The lower price is attractive too, but in the end, the Monarch UX kept me hooked. Still, for families who want straightforward budgeting without extra bells and whistles, Simplifi really shines. ## 4\. Crew ![](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/crew-app-and-debit-card.png) Crew takes the classic envelope budgeting method and gives it a modern twist. Families can create digital “pockets” for everything from groceries to clothing, while kids get their own debit cards and learn to manage money early. Parents can pay allowances or even compensate kids for helping out with family business tasks, all directly through the app. **Best Features** - Digital envelope budgeting through “pockets” - High-yield checking and savings available for adults and kids ( _**3.45% APY**_) - Family accounts with shared access - Kids’ debit cards, pockets, and allowances - Easy allowance and chore payments **Things to Consider** - Best suited for families who budget with debit cards, not credit cards - Still building out features like deeper goal tracking and mobile check deposit - Not a bank itself — works with Bangor Savings Bank (FDIC insured) **Price** - Free basic plan 👉 [Start with Crew’s **free plan** today](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/crew) (Get an additional 0.5% APY with my partner link) 👉 Want a deeper dive? [Read our full Crew Review](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/crew-review-family-banking/). **Personal Note** For full transparency, I’m such a fan of Crew that I became a **minority shareholder in the company**. My kids, Zoey and Calvin, already use Crew to manage their clothing, giving, and saving pockets. Calvin even saved up enough for his first pair of AirPods and bought them himself at Target. That independence and confidence with money is exactly why I believe Crew has so much potential. ## 5\. EveryDollar [![EveryDollar](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Screen-Shot-2022-09-19-at-2.55.31-PM-1024x565.jpg)](https://www.everydollar.com/) EveryDollar, created by Ramsey Solutions, is designed for people following Dave Ramsey’s financial principles. It works best for families who want a zero-based budget approach. **Best Features** - Personalized categories - Split transactions across multiple categories - Sync across devices - Savings goal tracking - Debt payoff tracking (premium version) **Things to Consider** - Free version requires manual transaction entry - No investment or credit score features **Price** - Free basic version - Premium: $17.99 per month or $79.99 annually 👉 [Try EveryDollar **free** (basic plan) or start a **14-day free trial** of Premium](https://www.ramseysolutions.com/money/everydollar) 👉 Want a deeper dive? [Read our full EveryDollar Review](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/everydollar-review-dave-ramsey-baby-steps/). **Personal Note** EveryDollar is especially helpful for those following Dave Ramsey’s Baby Steps. Nicole and I actually used this early in our financial journey, but it felt a little too restrictive for our style since we like cashback credit card rewards and have different investing philosophies than Ramsey. Still, Dave Ramsey, Ramsey Solutions, and EveryDollar remain excellent resources for millions of families who want a structured, debt-free path. ## 6\. Lunch Money ![Lunch Money](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/image.png) Lunch Money is a modern budgeting tool built for digital-first families. It handles multiple currencies, integrates with cryptocurrency wallets, and provides robust data insights. **Best Features** - Spending insights and analytics - Multi-currency support - Cryptocurrency integrations - Net worth tracking - iOS & Android companion app **Things to Consider** - Web-first platform (though a mobile companion app exists) **Price** - $10 per month or $100 annually 👉 [Try Lunch Money with a **free trial**](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/lunchmoney) 👉 Want a deeper dive? [Read our full Lunch Money Review](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/lunch-money-review/). **Personal Note** I’ve had the chance to get to know Jennifer Yip, the founder of Lunch Money. She started as a solopreneur and has grown it into a thriving business with an expanding team. The app has really taken off with people who need to track multiple currencies or want detailed spending insights. I think Lunch Money is only going to continue growing in the years ahead. ## 7\. Tiller [![Tiller](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Screen-Shot-2022-09-19-at-5.38.04-PM-1024x460.jpg)](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/tiller) Tiller is a spreadsheet-based budgeting tool that automates your financial tracking into Google Sheets or Excel. It’s perfect for spreadsheet lovers who want customization. **Best Features** - Multiple budget templates - Automated transaction imports - Custom categories and dashboards - Zero-sum budgeting option - No ads **Things to Consider** - Spreadsheet-focused — not a traditional app - Mobile access limited to Sheets/Excel apps **Price** - $79 per year (after a 30-day free trial) 👉 [Try Tiller **free for 30 days**](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/tiller) 👉 Want a deeper dive? [Read our full Tiller Money Review](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/tiller-money-review/). **Personal Note** I’ve interviewed and met with Tiller’s founder, Peter Polson. He’s a husband, father, and genuine community builder who leads a great remote team. His heart is in this product, and it shows. If you’re into spreadsheets and want automation without losing customization, Tiller is a fantastic choice. ## 8\. Origin ![](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/origin-app-662x1024.jpeg) Origin is a newer tool that blends budgeting with financial wellness. Creating your own spreadsheet for budgeting is completely free, highly customizable, and can help families stay very intentional about their money. **Best Features** - 100% customizable to your needs - Free (just use Google Sheets or Excel) - Forces you to engage with your money manually - Can be shared with your partner **Things to Consider** - No automation — all transactions must be entered manually - Can be time-consuming if you have lots of accounts - Requires some comfort with spreadsheets **Price** - Free 👉 [Get started with Google Sheets — it’s **free**](https://workspace.google.com/products/sheets/) **Personal Note** While I use automated budgeting apps personally, I also keep a Google Sheet budget as a broad overview of where our family spending should be. # Best Software for Parents to Track Their Children’s Financial Learning Progress

- by [Loral Langemeier](https://lorallangermeiergrant.com/author/loral-langemeier/ "Posts by Loral Langemeier")
- December 4, 2025December 4, 2025

![Parent and child reviewing a money-management app together at a clean, modern home desk.](https://lorallangermeiergrant.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Best-Software-for-Parents-to-Track-Their-Childrens-Financial-Learning-Progress.jpeg)

You can track your children’s [financial learning](https://www.investopedia.com/guide-to-financial-literacy-4800530) progress effectively by using software designed to monitor allowance, spending, saving, and [goal-setting habits](https://jamesclear.com/goal-setting). The right tools help you guide their money decisions with clarity and consistency.

This article gives you the leading software options parents use to supervise financial learning at home. You’ll understand how each tool works, when it fits best, and how to use these platforms to build strong money habits that grow with your child.

## **App 1: Greenlight — A Complete Financial Learning System for Kids and Teens**

Greenlight gives you a powerful combination of oversight, safety, and independence for your child. It provides a debit card for kids and teens, real-time parental controls, instant transfer options, and clear visibility into every transaction.

You set allowance schedules, spending limits, and location-based usage rules. When your child makes a purchase, you receive an alert immediately. This direct connection between your supervision and their actions helps reinforce accountability. Kids also learn real-world budgeting because they use their Greenlight card for actual purchases, not simulated money.

Greenlight includes features for savings, chores, and [optional investing](https://www.investopedia.com/options-basics-tutorial-4583012). When your child sets a savings goal, the app tracks progress visually. That creates discipline around delayed gratification. As children move into their teen years, you can expand their responsibilities or adjust controls gradually.

## **App 2: BusyKid — A Chore-Driven Allowance System That Teaches Responsibility**

BusyKid helps children understand that money is earned. The app connects chores to allowance so your child experiences income as a direct result of effort. You assign tasks, set payouts, and approve completions through the parent dashboard.

This structure reflects how income works in the real world. Kids complete tasks, get paid, and decide how to allocate their earnings. BusyKid encourages splitting income into categories like spending, saving, or giving. This early version of money allocation helps children form habits that remain useful well into adulthood.

Because BusyKid offers debit-card features, your child gains experience handling small purchases in controlled environments. You still supervise all activity while helping them practise responsible decision-making. It’s a strong solution when your goal is to build accountability, routine, and structured financial behavior.

## **App 3: Rooster Money — Best for Early-Stage Learning and Habit Building**

Rooster Money works well when your child is young and just starting to explore how money works. The interface is simple enough for beginners, but meaningful enough to reinforce important lessons.

You assign allowances, track chores, and help your child visualize savings jars. Kids learn to watch their balance increase and decrease. They understand that spending reduces their total and that savings require patience. These foundational lessons prepare them for more advanced financial tools later.

Because Rooster Money allows you to separate money into jars, it naturally teaches planning. If your child wants something, they can allocate part of their allowance toward the goal and monitor progress. This reinforces positive behaviors before you introduce more complex features like debit cards or budgeting categories.

## **App 4: KidBudget — Manual Tracking for Early Cash-Based Allowances**

KidBudget supports parents who prefer to introduce financial learning without connecting to banking systems. It functions as a digital ledger for allowances, spending, and savings.

You input allowance amounts manually, record purchases, and update savings totals. This hands-on method strengthens awareness because your child must participate in logging their actions. When they see their balance updated after every spending choice, they begin associating decisions with consequences.

KidBudget suits children who still receive cash gifts or cash allowance. Its simplicity avoids overwhelming younger learners while still reinforcing clarity and structure. When kids show readiness, you can graduate them to apps with more autonomy.

## **App 5: Shared-Expense Tools — Teaching Fairness and Group Responsibility**

Shared-expense features help children understand cooperation, planning, and fairness. These tools are ideal for siblings sharing costs, group gifts, school outings, or collective expenses.

You document each child’s contributions and spending. Kids learn that shared purchases require communication and accountability. This skill becomes valuable as they navigate friendships, classroom groups, and eventually adult financial situations like roommates or group projects.

By pairing a shared-expense tool with a primary allowance application, you support both individual discipline and collaborative responsibility. Children see how money affects relationships and why clear tracking matters.

## **What parents should look for in financial learning software?**

You should choose software that balances independence and supervision. The ideal tool gives your child enough freedom to make decisions while giving you enough visibility to intervene when needed.

Key features include allowance automation, chore tracking, savings goals, spending alerts, and parental approval settings. Younger children benefit from simpler dashboards while older kids benefit from debit-card systems that simulate real-world conditions.

Security matters as well. You want tools that offer account protection, secure transfers, and data-privacy controls. Reviewing transaction history regularly reinforces learning and helps you guide productive conversations around money.

## **Which apps work best for different age groups?**

Younger children need simplicity. Tools like Rooster Money or KidBudget introduce money management without complexity. They give kids an early sense of structure through allowances, chores, and simple savings goals.

As your child grows older, you shift to more advanced systems like BusyKid or Greenlight. These give real-world financial experience through debit cards, automated allowance deposits, spending limits, and even investing features. Teens benefit from this transition because they begin preparing for future financial independence.

The goal is progression. You start with basic awareness, move into structured habits, and eventually introduce autonomy under supervision. Matching the software to your child’s readiness ensures smoother learning curves.

## **How to reinforce financial learning using these apps?**

The app alone won’t shape your child’s habits. Your guidance creates the learning environment.

Use allowance day as a predictable moment to discuss decisions. Talk through savings goals and spending choices. Reinforce positive behavior like waiting to purchase something or meeting a chore completion schedule.

Tie money discussions to real-world situations your child understands. If they overspend and cannot meet a goal that month, guide them through alternatives. If they save consistently, celebrate the progress. Over time, the app becomes the structure and you become the coach.

## **Common concerns parents have when adopting these tools**

Many parents worry about overspending, complexity, or data safety. Good software resolves these concerns through spending caps, parental approval features, and secure systems.

You also want to avoid overwhelming young kids. Introduce features gradually. Start with allowance and savings only. Add chores, spending logs, or goals when your child shows responsibility.

Another concern is subscription cost. Some apps charge monthly fees, especially those offering debit cards. Review what your family needs before subscribing. Strong financial learning doesn’t require every premium feature — it requires consistency.

## **How to create a financial learning system at home using these tools**

To build a system that lasts, combine routine, clarity, and accountability. Establish a consistent allowance schedule. Assign age-appropriate chores. Help kids set one or two savings goals per month. Use software to track progress together.

Review the data weekly. Look for patterns in spending or saving. Encourage your child to reflect on what they achieved. These discussions build confidence and awareness.

## **Best apps for tracking kids’ financial learning**

- Greenlight for supervised debit-card learning
- BusyKid for chore-linked allowance
- Rooster Money for young beginners
- KidBudget for manual tracking
- Shared-expense tools for group learning

## **Start Building Strong Financial Habits at Home**

You now have a clear path to supporting your children’s financial education with structured tools and consistent guidance. The right software gives them responsibility, transparency, and real-world practice — all while you remain in control of the learning environment. Pair the app with conversations, routines, and thoughtful supervision to create habits that stay with them into adulthood. When financial learning becomes part of family life, kids grow confident, capable, and prepared for future decisions.
